hook.text: The Model T wasn't the fastest or prettiest car in 1908. It was the toughest.

buildup.text: Ford designed it to survive unpaved farm roads, with high clearance and simple parts anyone could fix.

discovery.text: It ran on gasoline, kerosene, or even ethanol—farmers loved that flexibility.

twist.text: Ford offered it in any color—as long as it was black. Black paint dried fastest on the line.

climax.text: The price dropped from $850 to $260 over its life, making it cheaper than a horse and buggy.

punchline.text: The Model T made the car a tool, not a toy.

quiz.question: Why was the Model T only available in black?
